title: Anthropic Releases Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 Ahead of IPO
excerpt: The new Claude models run up to 30% faster and cost 20% less, with Fable open to all users and Mythos restricted to vetted organisations, days before a Wall Street debut targeted for the week of November 16.
body:
• Anthropic on Monday released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which the company says generate outputs up to 30% faster than their predecessors and cost 20% less.
  • Pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens; Fable 5.2 is generally available, while Mythos 5.2 is restricted to vetted organisations in life sciences and cybersecurity.
  • The launch is Anthropic's first frontier-model release since CEO Dario Amodei publicly called for a slowdown in AI development in September.
  • Anthropic is aiming to hold its IPO the week of November 16, at a valuation reported at $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion, down from a $2 trillion figure floated in recent months.

Anthropic announced on Monday that it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, as the company prepares for a highly anticipated initial public offering this month, AFP reported. The company said the models can perform up to 30% faster than previous versions, particularly on complex tasks such as coding, while costing 20% less.

Same underlying model, two different rulebooks

Both models are built on the same underlying system, and they diverge on safeguards. Fable 5.2 carries safeguards that block most cybersecurity and biology tasks, which lets Anthropic offer it to all users; it became generally available on Monday. Mythos 5.2 has fewer of those restrictions and is available only to vetted organisations working in cybersecurity or biomedical research, through Anthropic's Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs. Pricing for the generation starts at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, down from the 5.1 generation's $10 and $50, with an optional fast mode at $16 and $80.

The first versions of Fable and Mythos were released under a cloud of controversy. Both models were pulled days after their June launch, when the US Commerce Department, citing national security concerns, ordered Anthropic to bar access by foreign nationals; the controls were lifted weeks later.

An IPO that will test the AI boom

The launch lands days before the company's Wall Street debut. Anthropic is aiming to hold its IPO the week of November 16, when AFP reported it is expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would make it the largest IPO on record. CNBC has reported the company is targeting a valuation of $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion, down from a $2 trillion target floated in recent months. The stock market debut is being watched as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom can last.

The filing figures behind the debut are stark. Anthropic's revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed, though sales growth slowed from previous quarters amid competition from OpenAI and cheaper models, many from China. The company also posted an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter as it paid more for short-term computing capacity. Dianne Penn, Anthropic's head of product management for research, told CNBC the company intends to maintain development while addressing safety concerns — a balance that also features in the risk disclosures in its amended IPO prospectus.

What to watch

Formal marketing for the offering opens this week, and the final IPO price range — still blank in the filing as of Monday — will show how much of the earlier $2 trillion ambition public investors are willing to underwrite. For users, the immediate change is simpler: Fable 5.2 is live today at a lower price, and Mythos 5.2 stays behind a vetting gate. Read the AFP report via TechXplore.
